summary: ACCEPT. Fixes the P0 found live this morning: the v2 boot hold could not release on a pre-market boot, suppressing entries fleet-wide with no timeout. ROOT CAUSE, confirmed at bot.py:2029-2036 before any fix was written: the ONLY entry into _rest_warmup_done was a REST callback carrying a bar younger than 300s, and the docstring directly above stated the assumption -- 'REST is the only live feed'. That assumption is FALSE in the deployed architecture: the STREAMER is the live feed and REST backfills history, so REST's newest bar is always older and in pre-market is DAYS older. The latch used 'a fresh REST bar arrived' as a proxy for 'this symbol is ready', and the proxy is structurally unreachable whenever pricehistory has no same-day data. THE EVIDENCE FIT EXACTLY: confirmed=2 (DB history seeded, gate 2 PASSED), rest_warmed=0 across 136/136 numeric observations, 676 REST bars delivered for AEHL (replay WORKED), streamer alive and arming WBUY, all three REST batches ending on Friday bars. Nothing was broken except the freshness proxy. THE FIX IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND THE LAYERING IS WHAT MAKES IT SAFE: the timeout releases ONLY the warmup proxy. It drains pending streamer bars, caps reconstructed segments, and THE DANGEROUS-SEGMENT BOOT HOLD STILL RUNS AFTERWARDS and may continue to suppress entries. ⭐ That is why an n=1 constant is acceptable here: a too-short value costs SUPPRESSED entries, never UNSAFE ones. VERIFIED BY EXECUTED MUTATION ACROSS TWO ROUNDS, in an isolated worktree with module provenance proven first. ROUND 1, baseline 72: M-A removing 'not selected.issubset(self._db_seeded)' -- the guard that stops a timeout releasing without DB history -- DIED, killed by test_warmup_timeout_cannot_release_an_unconfirmed_seed. That is the guard that matters most and it held from the start. ⛔ M-B removing the population-unchanged reset SURVIVED with 72 passed. That was not theoretical: TODAY'S OWN EVENT EXERCISED IT -- AEHL was added at 04:06 ET and YDDL at 05:28 ET, so the selected population CHANGED MID-WAIT. Without the reset, a clock started by one symbol set can expire against a different set that has waited seconds. The code comment claimed the property and no test defended it. ROUND 2, baseline 73, source BYTE-IDENTICAL to the reviewed head (0 files changed under src/, 51 test lines added): M-B replay DIED, killed by test_warmup_timeout_restarts_when_selected_population_changes. ⭐ M-C, which I INVENTED AFTER the correction so it cannot have been written to -- deleting the elapsed < TIMEOUT check so the timeout fires immediately -- DIED, killing TWO tests including test_seeded_warmup_timeout_is_bounded_and_distinct. Restore hash-verified byte-identical at 03908bb83ecf4824. ON THE 369s CONSTANT: accepted with codex's own framing kept verbatim -- it is honest that it is n=1 and 'an exposure-calibrated safety-policy bound, not a REST-latency claim', with 'another observed exceedance is a measured re-calibration item'. That is the correct way to carry a single-observation constant. ⚠️ OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE RECORDED IN THE PR BODY AT MY REQUEST: on a pre-market boot the TIMEOUT, not REST, becomes the usual release path. Today the wait population stabilised at 05:28 with both symbols seeded, so a 369s timeout would have fired around 05:34 -- roughly 87 minutes BEFORE the natural release at 07:01:09. A future reader must not mistake a timeout release for a REST success. NOT MEASURED: I ran the two focused test files, not the full suite; codex reports 2,950 passed with 14 skipped plus 31 replay/backtest, taken on report. I did not mutate the streamer-drain or segment-capping paths on the timeout branch. ⛔ MY OWN ERROR THAT CAUSED THIS EXPOSURE, on record: my #827 pin stated 'a weekend restart CANNOT converge... which would push the first convergence test into Monday's unattended pre-market open.' I wrote that, then authorized two weekend restarts -- lifting my own #843 hold and deploying #848/#849 on Sunday. This morning is that prediction coming true. The deploy path should encode the no-pre-market-boot rule rather than rely on either agent remembering it. ⛔ DEPLOY: src/** => v2-only restart, AFTER THE CLOSE or the normal pre-open window. Production self-resolved at 07:01:09 ET and total exposure was about 69 seconds, so there is no urgency; a mid-day restart would suspend live entries and re-run the whole boot-hold cycle to fix something that cost one minute. Run the bar-continuity checklist for REAL -- the market is open and this is a genuine bar-hole risk, not N/A-weekend.
